questions.question: The definition of small appliance lists room air conditioners as an example. Which kind of equipment does it name as included among room air conditioners?

options.A: MVAC-like appliances
options.C: Packaged terminal air heat pumps
options.D: Industrial process refrigeration

questions.explanation: The definition lists "room air conditioners (including window air conditioners, portable air conditioners, and packaged terminal air heat pumps)." MVACs and MVAC-like appliances are separate categories with their own rules, and industrial process refrigeration is not named in the small appliance definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: room air conditioners (including window air conditioners, portable air conditioners, and packaged terminal air heat pumps), dehumidifiers, under-the-counter ice makers, vending machines, and drinking water coolers.

questions.question: The definition of small appliance names refrigerators and freezers designed for which uses?

options.A: Home, commercial, or consumer use
options.C: Commercial use only
options.D: Military use only

questions.explanation: The definition includes "refrigerators and freezers (designed for home, commercial, or consumer use)." It is not limited to home or commercial units alone.

questions.question: Which refrigerant, when used in household refrigerators and freezers, is listed as exempt from the venting prohibition and the requirements of Subpart F?

options.A: HCFC-22
options.C: HFC-134a
options.D: Isobutane (R-600a)

questions.explanation: The exempt list includes "Isobutane (R-600a) in retail food refrigerators and freezers (stand-alone units only); household refrigerators, freezers, and combination refrigerators and freezers; and vending machines." HFC-134a is not on the exempt list, so it is a non-exempt substitute, and CFC-12 and HCFC-22 are ozone-depleting refrigerants covered by the rule.

questions.question: Propane (R-290) is exempt from the venting prohibition and the requirements of Subpart F in certain end-uses. Which of these end-uses is on that list?

options.A: Motor vehicle air conditioners
options.C: MVAC-like appliances
options.D: Comfort-cooling chillers

questions.explanation: The propane exemption covers end-uses including vending machines, "self-contained commercial ice machines, very low temperature refrigeration equipment, and water coolers." Motor vehicle air conditioners, MVAC-like appliances and chillers are not in the propane list.

questions.question: Under Appendix D, which test formats may an organization that provides only Type I certification choose from?

options.A: Either an on-site format or a mail-in format
options.C: Only an oral format
options.D: Only a closed-book test at an EPA office

questions.explanation: Appendix D says "organizations providing Type I certification only may choose either an on-site format or a mail-in format." The program may pick either one, so it is not limited to mail-in, oral or EPA-office testing.

questions.question: A technician paints a household refrigerator. How does the technician definition classify painting the appliance?

options.A: As opening the appliance
options.C: As an activity not reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit
options.D: As work that only a Type I technician may perform

questions.explanation: The rule says activities "such as painting the appliance, rewiring an external electrical circuit, replacing insulation on a length of pipe, or tightening nuts and bolts are not reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit." Painting does not release refrigerant, so it is not opening or disposal.

questions.question: According to the technician definition, activities on an appliance that has been properly evacuated under 40 CFR 82.156 are not reasonably expected to release refrigerants unless the activity includes what?

options.A: Painting the appliance
options.C: Rewiring an external electrical circuit
options.D: Adding refrigerant to the appliance

questions.explanation: Activities on properly evacuated appliances "are not reasonably expected to release refrigerants unless the activity includes adding refrigerant to the appliance." Painting, tightening nuts and bolts and rewiring an external circuit are listed as activities not expected to violate the refrigerant circuit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, what must each test for Type I certification provide?

options.A: A copy of the EPA test bank
options.B: A means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test
options.C: A list of the correct answers for self-checking
options.D: A practice version of the test

questions.explanation: Appendix D states: "Each test for Type I certification must provide a means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test," such as a driver's license or passport. Appendix D also requires programs to keep test questions and answer keys confidential, so a test does not come with the question bank or its answers.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each test for Type I certification must provide a means of verifying the identification of the individual taking the test. Acceptable forms of identification include but are not limited to drivers' licenses and passports.

questions.question: A technician recovers refrigerant from a small appliance that contains a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute. Under 40 CFR 82.154(b)(2), the recovery and/or recycling equipment must be certified under 40 CFR 82.158 for what?

options.A: Any one refrigerant, which then covers all others
options.B: The refrigerant only, whatever the type of appliance
options.C: MVACs only
options.D: That type of refrigerant and appliance

questions.explanation: No one may service such an appliance without "using recovery and/or recycling equipment that is certified for that type of refrigerant and appliance under § 82.158." Certification for the refrigerant alone, or for MVACs, does not meet this rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Using recovery and/or recycling equipment that is certified for that type of refrigerant and appliance under § 82.158.

questions.question: A technician who passed a Type I test receives a wallet-sized certification card. The card must carry a unique number for the certified person. What must that number leave out?

options.A: The type of certification
options.C: The name of the certifying program
options.D: The technician's name

questions.explanation: The card must include "a unique number for the certified person that does not include a technician's social security number." The card must also show the certifying program's name, the person's name and the type of certification, so those are required, not left out.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A Type I program uses the mail-in format. By when must it issue a certification card to a technician who passed?

options.A: No later than 60 days from the date the technician mailed the test
options.B: No later than 30 days from the date the program receives the completed test and any required documentation
options.C: No later than 90 days from the date the program receives the completed test
options.D: No later than one year from the date of the test

questions.explanation: Mail-in Type I programs "must issue cards to certified technicians no later than 30 days from the date the certifying program receives the completed test and any required documentation." The 30 days run from receipt by the program, not from when the technician mailed the test.

questions.question: According to the proctoring section of Appendix D, in which case is the Type I certification test a closed-book exam?

options.A: Only when it is taken by mail
options.B: Only when the technician asks for an oral test
options.C: Only when the technician is an apprentice
options.D: When it is taken as part of a Universal certification

questions.explanation: Appendix D states that the test "for Type I (if taken as part of a Universal certification), Type II, Type III, and Universal technicians is a closed-book exam." It also says "Mail-in format Type I tests cannot be used toward a Universal certification."

questions.question: For an in-person Type I test, how many registered proctors must a certifying program designate?

options.A: At least one for every 10 people testing at the same time at a site
options.B: At least one for every 25 people testing at the same time at a site
options.C: At least one for every 50 people testing at the same time at a site
options.D: At least one for every 100 people testing at the same time at a site

questions.explanation: A program for "Type I (if in-person)" and the other types must designate "at least one proctor registered for every 50 people taking tests at the same time at a given site." The rule does not use a 10, 25 or 100 person ratio.

questions.question: Appendix D lists the subject areas for Group II, the sector-specific questions on a Type I test. Which of these is one of them?

options.A: Shipping
options.C: Changing industry outlook
options.D: Environmental impact of CFCs, HCFCs, and substitute refrigerants

questions.explanation: Group II covers sector-specific issues in "Leak detection," "Recovery Techniques," "Safety," "Shipping" and "Disposal." Laws and regulations, industry outlook and environmental impact are the Group I (core) areas.

questions.question: Small-appliance recovery equipment made or imported before November 15, 1993, counts as certified if it can recover 80 percent of the refrigerant in the system under which test-stand condition?

options.A: Only with the test stand's compressor operational
options.B: Only with the test stand's compressor not operational
options.C: Whether or not the test stand's compressor is operational
options.D: Only when tested by the appliance manufacturer

questions.explanation: Equipment made or imported before that date "will be considered certified if it is capable of either recovering 80 percent of the refrigerant in the system, whether or not the compressor of the test stand is operational," or of achieving a four-inch vacuum. The split of 90 percent with the compressor operational and 80 percent when it is not is the general appendix C standard in 82.158(e).

questions.question: Equipment used to evacuate a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute from small appliances before they are disposed of may also be certified if, tested with a properly calibrated pressure gauge, it can achieve what?

options.A: A four-inch vacuum
options.C: A one-inch vacuum
options.D: Recovery of 50 percent of the charge

questions.explanation: Such equipment "may also be certified if it is capable of achieving a four-inch vacuum when tested using a properly calibrated pressure gauge." The rule names a four-inch vacuum, not zero psig, a one-inch vacuum or a percentage of the charge.

questions.question: Besides the certification statement, what must the label on certified small-appliance recovery equipment show?

options.A: The technician's certification number
options.C: The date the equipment was last used
options.D: The date of manufacture and the serial number (if applicable)

questions.explanation: Labels on equipment certified under 82.158(d) and (e) "must also show the date of manufacture and the serial number (if applicable) of the equipment." The rule does not ask for a technician's number, an owner's details or a date of last use on the label.

questions.question: EPA's test method for recovery devices used with small appliances (appendix C) runs its tests at what temperature?

options.A: 32 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F
options.B: 75 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F
options.C: 104 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F
options.D: Any room temperature the laboratory chooses

questions.explanation: Appendix C states: "Tests are to be conducted at 75 degrees F, plus or minus 2 degrees F." The method sets a fixed temperature rather than leaving it to the laboratory.

questions.question: Which of these does the regulation's definition of disposal include?

options.A: Moving an appliance to a new room
options.C: Measuring an appliance's pressures with gauges
options.D: Recycling an appliance for scrap

questions.explanation: Disposal means the process leading to and including several listed activities, among them "the disassembly of any appliance for reuse of its component parts" and "the recycling of any appliance for scrap." Painting and measuring pressures are not on that list.

questions.question: A final processor uses a signed contract with a supplier of small appliances instead of signed statements. What must the contract do?

options.A: List the weight of refrigerant in each appliance
options.B: Be filed with EPA within 30 days
options.C: State that the supplier will recover any remaining refrigerant before delivery, or verify that the refrigerant was properly recovered before the supplier received the appliances
options.D: Name the testing organization that certified the recovery machine

questions.explanation: A signed contract "must either state that the supplier will recover any remaining refrigerant" before delivery "or verify that the refrigerant had been properly recovered prior to receipt by the supplier." The rule does not require refrigerant weights, a filing with EPA or the name of a testing organization.

questions.question: A final processor must tell its suppliers that refrigerant must be properly recovered before delivery. What form may that notice take?

options.A: Signs, letters to suppliers, or other equivalent means
options.B: Only a notice published in the Federal Register
options.C: Only a report filed with EPA
options.D: Only a notice on the technician's certification card

questions.explanation: The rule says "the form of this notification may be signs, letters to suppliers, or other equivalent means." It does not require a Federal Register notice or an EPA filing.

questions.question: When is it a violation for a final processor to accept a signed statement or contract about refrigerant recovery?

options.A: When the final processor knew or had reason to know the statement or contract is false
options.B: Whenever the supplier is not a certified technician
options.C: Whenever the statement is kept in electronic format
options.D: Whenever the appliance was delivered by a third party

questions.explanation: It is a violation to accept a signed statement or contract "if the person receiving the statement or contract knew or had reason to know that the signed statement or contract is false." The rule does not tie the violation to who delivered the appliance or whether the supplier is certified, and it allows the statements to be kept "in hard copy or in electronic format."
